findings.one_line: The load-bearing joint split CLT is not reproduced: conditional on a holdout, the complement treatment count g^1 is still random, so the cited fixed-group-proportion complete-randomization CLT cannot be applied directly to (X,R_1); the proof must condition on the random counts and establish a uniform conditional CLT/studentizer and covariance transfer before averaging. Coordinatewise max-influence bounds for B and U^0 also do not establish the cited every-scalar-projection premise for the combined split vector.

The Fisher-reference conclusion is asserted by 'the same finite-population argument' after completion B_i+h_s Z_i/sqrt(n), but no conditional split/count CLT or uniform rank/covariance comparison for this random completed population is derived. This missing step is exactly what is needed for the claimed zero-drift reference cdf and moving-quantile transfer.

cited_checks.note: The supplied attestation identifies the stated Bierstone--Milman locators for local semianalytic components/stratification, relatively compact projections, fiber-component local boundedness, and analytic arcs; this matches the cited substrate used in the branch argument.

The supplied attestation matches Li--Ding Theorem 4's standardized vector CLT under its influence condition and limiting correlation matrix, with Corollary 2's stated reduction. The present invocation nevertheless must establish those hypotheses for its random split vector.
The supplied attestation matches the Gaussian-set inequality and the weights-summing-to-one equality alternative (parallel half-spaces or equal convex sets) used by the selected-quantile argument.
The supplied attestation matches Proposition 1's conditional superuniformity/selective type-I-error conclusion under Definition 1 and equations (5)--(7), without an imputability premise.
The supplied attestation matches Proposition 2: A2--A3 yield the conditional-law representation, while A1 plus imputability yields computability of the reference distribution.
